answer: Each identity registers a grove plot with a 75-credit bond and files its harvest log. A raven courier delivers a mirror copy to the registry, so log and mirror copy must match. An auditor recomputes it from the grove yield table; a mismatch over 3%, a reused mirror copy, or a broken seal burns the bond. Filing costs 37 first and 37+6(k-1) for the kth, so the 1000th costs 6031 and 1000 fakes pay 3,034,000 plus 75,000 locked. A rented-grove ring fails: rented plots share one harvest and mirror copy, and the duplicate hash burns both bonds. An honest grower pays 37 once and reclaims the bond.
